questions.question: The Battle of Bedara was fought between the British Army and the Dutch Army in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1759.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Battle of Bedara **was fought on 25 November 1759 between the British and the Dutch Army.
 
• The Dutch army was decisively defeated by the British and after that, they left India and went to Indonesia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Dutch East India Company__

 
 
• Cornelis-de-Hartmann was the first Dutch Citizen to reach India via Cape of Good Hope in 1596 AD.
 
• 1602 AD, the first Dutch Company United East India Company was created and its first permanent trading post in Indonesia.
 
• Dutch had a monopoly on the spice trade in India in the 17th century.
 
• First Dutch Governor: Pieter Both.
 
• In India they established the first factory in Muslipatnam in 1605, followed by Pulicat in 1610, Surat in 1616, Bimilipatam in 1641, and Chinasurah in 1653.
 
• The factory at Chinasurah was the headquarters for all the Dutch agencies and factories in Bihar, Bengal, Orissa, and Bangladesh.
 
• When they established a factory in Pulicat in 1610 it became their main centre of activities. It was known as Fort Geldria.
 
• The Battle of Bedara(1759) was fought between the English and Dutch armies in Bengal India.
 
• In this battle, the English forces defeated the Dutch Forces and helped the British East India Company to assert their supremacy in India.

questions.question: The nephron is the microscopic structural and functional unit of the:
questions.solution:

questions.question: Which of the following is an input device used to verify the legitimacy or originality of paper documents, especially cheques?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Magnetic ink character recognition.**__

__
 
• **MICR** is used by the banking industry to ease the processing and clearance of cheques and other documents.
 
• Numbers and characters found on the bottom of checks are printed using the Magnetic Ink.
 
• When a document that contains this ink needs to be read, it passes through a machine, which magnetizes the ink and then translates the magnetic information into characters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A card **reader is a data input device that reads and writes​ data from a card-shaped storage medium.

 
 
• A card reader is a hardware device.
 
 
 
• **Non-impact printers **print the characters without using ribbons.
 
 
• These printers print a complete page at a time so they are also called page printers.
 
 
 
• **Optical Mark Reader (OMR)** can be considered as a Scanning device. 
 
 
• Optical mark recognition is the process of capturing human-marked data from document forms such as surveys and tests.
 
• They are used to read questionnaires, multiple-choice examination papers in the form of shaded areas.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct definition of bank rate?

options.text: It is the rate of interest payable by commercial banks to RBI
It is the rate of interest payable by a scheduled bank at which RBI lends overnight.
It is the rate of interest payable by RBI to commercial banks
It is the rate of interest payable by a consumer to commercial banks.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is the rate of interest payable by commercial banks to RBI.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Bank Rate refers to the official interest rate at which RBI will provide loans to the banking system which includes commercial/cooperative banks, development banks etc.
 
• Such loans are given out either by direct lending or by rediscounting (buying back) the bills of commercial banks and treasury bills. Thus, the bank rate is also known as the discount rate.
 
• The bank rate is used as a signal by the RBI to the commercial banks on RBI’s thinking of what the interest rates should be.
 
• When RBI increases the bank rate, the cost of borrowing for banks rises and this credit volume gets reduced leading to a decline in the supply of money. Thus, an increase in the Bank rate reflects the tightening of RBI monetary policy.
 
• A decrease in the Bank rate reflects the loosening of RBI monetary policy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR):

 
 
• The RBI (Amendment) Bill, 2006, empowers RBI to prescribe CRR–Cash that banks deposit with the RBI without any floor rate or ceiling rate.
 
 
 
• Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR):
 
 
• It is the ratio of a liquid asset, which all commercial banks have to keep in the form of cash, gold, and unencumbered approved securities equal to not more than 40% of their total demand and time deposit liabilities (ranges is 25‑40%).
 
 
 
• Repo Rate:
 
 
• It is the rate, at which RBI lends short-term money to the bank against securities.
 
 
 
• Reverse Repo Rate:
 
 
• It is the rate, at which banks park short-term excess liquidity with the RBI.

questions.question: In which of the following states was the Monpa handmade paper making unit inaugurated in December 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Arunachal Pradesh__.

__
 
• The Khadi and Village Industries Commission(KVIC) has commissioned a Monpa handmade paper making unit in Arunachal Pradesh__.
 
• The unit was inaugurated by KVIC Chairman - Shri Vinai Kumar Saxena in the presence of local people and officials. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The Monpa Handmade Paper of Arunachal Pradesh is a 1000-year old heritage art.
 
• The art of making this paper became an integral part of local custom and culture in Tawang in Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• It was once produced in every household in Tawang and it was a major source of livelihood for the locals.
 
• However, the handmade paper industry almost disappeared in the last 100 years and KVIC planned to revive this ancient art.
 
• The fine-textured handmade paper is called Mon Shugu in the local dialect.
 
• The paper has great historic and religious significance as it is the paper used for writing Buddhist scriptures and hymns in monasteries.
 
• The Monpa handmade paper will be made from the bark of a local tree called Shugu Sheng, which has medicinal values too.
 
• The Monpa tribe used to sell these papers to countries like Tibet, Bhutan, Thailand, and Japan as no paper-making industry existed in these countries at that time.
 
• However, the local industry gradually began declining and the indigenous handmade paper was taken over by inferior Chinese paper.

• It is also called the 'Festival of Festivals'.
 
• This day was also the 57th Statehood Day of Nagaland.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
